mutations.because: The D210(c) oracle, on the route whose 404 body a caller can read back through an attack. Removing this branch lets the plain CampaignNotFoundError branch answer instead, and because BriefRefNotFoundError is a SUBCLASS of it that is exactly what happens: no status change, no other check disturbed, and the body names the campaign the error carries - template.id, the source SLUG - rather than the ref the CALLER sent. A caller outside a team can then probe for that team's campaigns: duplicate a source addressed by uuid whose brief names assets/inputs/their-campaign/logo.png, and the refusal answers Brief their-campaign not found. when that campaign exists and Brief my-own-uuid not found. when it does not. That is the guessable-slug oracle D210(c) exists to close, and the mutant is well camouflaged because it is five lines shorter, still answers 404, and leaves the plain branch doing the right thing for the off-s3 backends. It is also invisible to a SLUG-addressed request - both bodies then carry the same string - which is why this lane's matrix addresses every source by uuid, and why the mutation is worth keeping: it is what proves the uuid is what the comparison turns on.
